Paragraph:
Translation: All living bodies subsist on food grains, which are produced from rain. Rains are produced by performance of yajna [sacrifice], and yajna is born of prescribed duties.

Purport (Excerpt): ...The material world is full of contaminations, and one who is immunized by accepting prasadam of the Lord... is saved from the attack... Food grains or vegetables are factually eatables... Ultimately, we have to depend on the production of the field... Yajna, specifically the sankirtana-yajna prescribed for this age, must therefore be performed...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Understanding the systemic chain of cause-and-effect that maintains biological and ecological life.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna outlines the cosmic wheel of life: Beings depend on food → Food depends on rain → Rain depends on sacrifice → Sacrifice depends on duty.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna sees that individual duty is directly linked to the survival and flourishing of the whole ecosystem.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Systems Thinking: Recognizing one's place within a complex, interconnected web of life
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Cause-and-Effect Awareness: Understanding how small, disciplined duties ripple through larger systems
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Sense of Belonging: Finding personal purpose by contributing to cosmic and social order

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Cakra (The cyclical wheel of cosmic interdependence)
Annad bhavanti bhutani (All living beings subsist on food grains)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Krishna illustrates the cosmic cycle: life relies on food, food on rain, rain on sacrifice, and sacrifice on prescribed action. Performing duty maintains this sacred wheel, sustaining both individual life and universal balance.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Recognizing systems thinking helps reduce feeling isolated or insignificant. Understanding that your daily actions contribute to a larger chain of cause-and-effect grants personal meaning and highlights the importance of keeping up your routine habits.
